THE HEADLINES: –

 

 

 

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, ongoing global crises highlighted clean energy as key to ensuring future energy and economic security; Says, country working towards 500-gigawatt renewable energy target by 2030.
  2. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says, government to continue prioritising capital spending to maintain growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline.
  3. Home Minister Amit Shah orders setting up of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices in all state capitals by next year.
  4. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu likely to make landfall near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh between midnight and early hours tomorrow; Andhra Pradesh and Odisha step up evacuation and disaster preparedness measures.
  5. Youth Olympics Games, Judoka Khushbu Darjada assures India of a medal by reaching Women’s 63kg final in Senegal; Dhinidhi Desinghu becomes first Indian female swimmer to qualify for the final.

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said, the ongoing global crises have highlighted that energy security was directly linked to economic security. He emphasised that the future of energy and economic security lies in clean energy. Mr Modi was addressing the gathering after inaugurating the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this evening.

 

 

         

Mr Modi said, the global economy faced unprecedented crises over the past few years, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to the ongoing crisis in West Asia. He said it is a matter of pride that India, with a population of 140 crore, effectively navigated these global challenges while sustaining high economic growth. He said, the country was firmly progressing towards its target of achieving 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based energy capacity by 2030.

 

 

 

         

The Prime Minister observed that the next phase of the solar revolution will depend not only on wider adoption but also on innovation.   He stressed the need to bring every government building, school, college, hospital and street-lighting system under solar power.
         

 

Speaking on the occasion, New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi said the sector had attracted investments worth 67 billion US dollars over the past two years.

 

 

         

 

On the occasion, Prime Minister Modi also visited various exhibition stalls and interacted with exhibitors. The theme of the four-day Summit is ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire’. It is witnessing participation from more than 130 countries, including over 40 ministers.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said, the government will continue to prioritise capital expenditure to sustain India’s growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline. Ms Sitharaman was speaking at a private event in Mumbai today. She said capital expenditure had delivered good results over the past four to five years through its multiplier effect and will remain an important part of the government’s growth strategy. She also identified credit access, insurance and pensions as priorities for the next phase of financial inclusion.

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

 

Home Minister Amit Shah has directed that Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) be established in all state capitals by next year. At present, FRRO offices are operational in 20 states. According to the Home Ministry, the number of foreign nationals visiting India for tourism, medical treatment and education has increased substantially, creating the need to expand the FRRO network across the country. The Ministry said, the Central Government is pursuing the establishment of FRROs in the remaining nine states: Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Meghalaya. More from our correspondent.

 

 

         

 

“The establishment of these FRRO offices will help foreigners visiting India in obtaining various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with State authorities and facilitate legitimate foreign visitors. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful stay of foreign nationals visiting or residing in India. Overall, the FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases of overstay and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalties where necessary. Anand Kumar, Akashvani News Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

The Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over the Bay of Bengal is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole between midnight tonight and early hours tomorrow. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, the cyclone will cross Andhra Pradesh coast with wind speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour, gusting up to 120 kilometres per hour, at the time of landfall, bringing heavy rainfall.

 

 

         

 

The governments of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up evacuation efforts and disaster preparedness measures to deal with the cyclone.
         

 

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed all government departments to remain on high alert and take necessary precautionary measures to minimise the loss of life and damage to property. More from our correspondent:

 

 

         

 

“Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is expected across coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema. Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram districts are likely to receive the highest rainfall. Chief Minister N.Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness with senior officials and district collectors. The government has mobilised 724 medical teams, 4,628 emergency beds, 205 relief camps and hundreds of ambulances. Electricity restoration teams, equipment and additional personnel from Chennai are being deployed. Officials have been directed to safeguard tanks and reservoirs, prevent flooding and restore essential services within 48 hours. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while people are urged to stay indoors and follow official warnings. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

         

 

In Odisha, around one lakh fifty thousand people have been evacuated from vulnerable areas and shifted to shelters and other safer locations. The fresh weather threat comes at a time when several parts of southern Odisha are still struggling to recover from the impact of Cyclone Arnab. Our correspondent has the details:

 

 

         

“Southern Odisha is once again facing a serious weather challenge due to serious cyclonic storm Murasu, particularly in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri and Kalahandi. Around one lakh fifty thousand people have been evacuated to cyclone shelters and other safer locations. NDRF and ODRAF teams, along with Fire Services personnel, have been deployed in vulnerable areas to undertake rescue and relief operations. Schools in vulnerable districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after. With the region still struggling to recover from Cyclone Arnab and the devastating floods, Murasu poses another major challenge for the State administration. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Ahead of the festival of Diwali, which falls on the 8th of this month, the Supreme Court has permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during specified hours on the 7th and 8th of November. The apex court further ordered that the complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, imposed earlier, will come back into force from the 9th of November.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has invoked all measures under Stage Two of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across the entire National Capital Region. The decision was taken after Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 324 today, placing it in the very poor category. Under Stage Two of GRAP, concerned agencies have been directed to intensify mechanical and vacuum-based road sweeping, along with regular water sprinkling and the use of dust suppressants. The measures also include increasing parking charges to discourage the use of private vehicles.
         

 

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has announced that it will operate 20 additional train trips on weekdays from tomorrow following the implementation of GRAP-2 in Delhi.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

The Bharatiya Janata Party conducted a “Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao” foot march campaign across the country to counter protests and allegations of the opposition parties. As part of the campaign, Senior BJP leader Amit Shah addressed a massive public rally in Hyderabad. He strongly criticised the Congress party over its recent political rallies, accusing it of attempting to protect illegal infiltrators rather than creating genuine awareness about voter rights. Mr Shah asserted that no illegal infiltrator will be allowed to exercise voting rights.

         

 

The Jharkhand unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party also launched its ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ foot march campaign in Ranchi.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21 thousand 800 crore rupees tomorrow afternoon through video conferencing. These projects will strengthen Pune’s public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Indian judoka Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada has assured the country of at least a medal at the Youth Olympic Games at Dakar in Senegal. 15-year-old Khushbu entered the final of the women’s 63-kilogram category, after defeating Algeria’s Dounia Berrahoual. She will now face Germany’s Jolina Reinhold, the reigning Cadet World Champion, in the gold medal match later tonight.
         

 

Meanwhile, Dhinidhi Desinghu has created history by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to qualify for the Youth Olympics final after advancing to women’s 100-metre freestyle medal race.  The 16-year-old from Bengaluru clocked 56.80 seconds to win her heat and finish third overall in the qualifying round.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

In the Men’s Hockey Asian Champions Trophy, India defeated South Korea by 8-Nil in the final league-stage match at Jalandhar in Punjab. In the first match of the day, China and Bangladesh played out a one-all draw. In the second match, Japan defeated Malaysia by, 2-1. From Wednesday, the semifinal stage will begin.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Benchmark domestic equity indices surged nearly 1.7 per cent today, extending their rally for the third consecutive session. The Sensex soared 1 thousand 233 points to close at 75 thousand 693. The Nifty climbed 388 points to settle at 23 thousand 441.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

In our bilingual live phone-in programme “Public Speak” tonight at 09.30 PM, we will bring an insightful Discussion on Khet Bachao Abhiyaan and the Future of Sustainable Agriculture with Dr Rajarshi Roy Burman, Assistant Director General (Agriculture Extension), ICAR. During the programme, listeners can ask questions on the subject. To participate, simply dial the telephone number 011-23310481, 011-23717117, 011-23717106 and 011-23314444  09:30 PM onwards tonight.

President Droupadi Murmu has said that every citizen has a responsibility to contribute to social welfare and national development. She called upon people to rise above personal interests and work for the larger good of society and the nation. The President was addressing a function marking the centenary of the sacrifice of Swami Shraddhanand at Gurukul in Haryana’s Kurukshetra, today. She stressed that collective efforts are essential to achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

 

 

Highlighting the life of Swami Shraddhanand, the President said he worked for social harmony and played an important role in India’s freedom struggle.

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

Earlier in the day, President Murmu addressed the Haryana Day celebrations in Kurukshetra, marking the 60th anniversary of the formation of the State. She said, the nationwide Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign has proved to be an important milestone in promoting women’s empowerment. She also said that Haryana had made remarkable progress over the past decade in various aspects of women’s empowerment.

 

Besides Haryana, several other states and Union Territories celebrated their formation day today. These include, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Punjab and Tamil Nadu. The President, Vice President and Prime Minister extended wishes to the people of these states and Union Territories on the occasion.

 

<><><> 

 

Union Home Minister Amit Shah today praised the Chandigarh Police for its courage and dedication in combating terrorism and maintaining law and order. He was addressing the 60th Raising Day celebrations of the Chandigarh Police in the city today.The Home Minister said the Chandigarh Police had displayed exceptional courage during the era of terrorism.

On the occasion, Mr Shah conferred the prestigious President’s Police Colour on the force. The honour was approved by President Droupadi Murmu. He also presented the President’s Medals to officers and personnel of the Chandigarh Police.

 

 

 

The Home Minister also flagged off 141 new vehicles for the Chandigarh Police.  Later, Mr Shah inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for several development projects worth 258 crore rupees in Chandigarh.

 

<><><> 

 

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit outlined his top priorities to strengthen and modernise the Indian Air force a day after taking charge as the 29th Chief of Air Staff. In his first address today, Indian Air Force Chief coined the guiding theme ‘VAYU’, articulating four distinct pillars that will shape the IAF’s future trajectory. These are Vigilance, Victory and Readiness, self-reliance, Yukti, and Unity of Effort. Through the ‘VAYU’ vision, Air Chief Marshal Dixit articulated a clear direction for an operationally ready, technologically advanced, self-reliant and seamlessly integrated Indian Air Force. He emphasised the need to maintain the highest level of operational preparedness across all formations, with restoring combat strength to sanctioned levels being a top priority.

 

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has hailed the inauguration of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Train which was flagged off by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that the Vande Bharat Sleeper Train will be a game changer for connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. The Prime Minister added that this train will benefit Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, especially benefitting youngsters, IT professionals and students. The train will cover the journey between the two cities in around 16 hours.

 

<><><> 

 

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal today intensified into a cyclone named as ‘Murasu, prompting Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up preparedness for another high-intensity storm in less than a week. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the latest storm is very likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm tomorrow morning.  It is likely to cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm between tomorrow midnight to early hours of Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph.

 

The IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh tomorrow. An orange alert has been issued Rayalaseema, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and Telangana tomorrow.

 

Heavy rainfall is also expected over Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Mahe, Odisha and South Interior Karnataka during the next two days.

Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is on high alert, with the state government stepping up precautionary measures to tackle the emerging threat. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm Murasu. It is moving west-northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning. It is expected to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur during the early hours of Wednesday, with wind speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the preparedness and directed departments to coordinate rescue and relief operations. Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams have been deployed. Control rooms have been set up, and evacuation of people from unsafe areas has been ordered. People have been urged to follow official warnings and contact 112 or 1070 for emergencies. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

 

 

Odisha is also preparing for another cyclonic storm, even as thousands of families continue to grapple with the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods. As a precautionary measure, authorities have also opened the gates of the Balimela reservoir. We have a report:

 

 

 

“Southern Odisha, still struggling to recover from the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods, is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall as Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ approaches the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department has forecast rainfall activity in Odisha starting tomorrow, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over southern districts on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput, Nowarangpur and Malkangiri are among the districts requiring close attention, particularly vulnerable hilly areas and flood-prone villages, where fresh rainfall could trigger flash floods and landslides. The state government has identified vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone locations, and initiated the evacuation of people to safer places. District Collectors of vulnerable areas have been kept on high alert. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

 

<><><> 

 

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the National Organ Transplant Games in New Delhi. Addressing the event, the Vice President described the Games as a celebration of the resilience of transplant recipients and demonstrating the life-transforming power of modern medicine.

 

 

 

On the occasion, Mr. Radhakrishnan witnessed an attempt to set a world record, featuring 570 transplant recipients and donors performing Tadasana together. Following the successful attempt, the organisers were presented with a certificate by the World Book of Records, New Delhi, for the ‘Largest Congregation of Transplant Recipients and Donors Performing Tadasana’.

 

<><><> 

 

The country’s gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections grew nearly 23 per cent year-on-year to over two lakh 31 thousand crore rupees in October this year. It was driven by robust domestic economic activity and a sharp rise in tax revenue from imports.

<><><> 

 

The Centre has withdrawn the special additional excise duty on petrol exports while increasing export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). Under the revised rates, petrol exports will attract no export duty, compared to the earlier levy of two rupees 50 paise per litre. The export duty on diesel has been increased from eight rupees 50 paise to 11 rupees 50 paise per litre while the levy on ATF has been raised from 10 rupees 50 paise to 11 rupees per litre.

<><><> 

 

In Badminton, two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has clinched the Women’s Singles title of Hylo Open Super 500 tournament in Germany today, her second title of the season. World No. 8 Sindhu defeated Denmark’s Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14 in the final. Earlier this year, Sindhu made history by winning the Japan Open.

Meanwhile, in the men’s singles final, Lakshya Sen will take on Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie in a short while.

 

<><><> 

 

In Archery, India has won four medals at the ongoing Swiss Open IWS Archery Championship in Switzerland. Sachin Chechi, Tania Rani and Priya Gurjar clinched silver medals, while Aditya Wadhwa secured bronze. Sachin won silver in the Compound Under-21 Men’s category after narrowly losing the final to Germany’s Simon Moritz by 145-147. In the Compound Under-21 Women’s category, Tania Rani also claimed silver after losing to Youth World Championship medallist Fenna Stallen in the final. Meanwhile, Priya Gurjar secured another silver medal in the Compound Women’s category. She lost to Mexico’s Andrea Maya Becerra Arizaga . In the Recurve Under-21 Men’s category, Aditya Wadhwa clinched bronze. He defeated Slovenia’s Gal Frank 6-2 in the bronze medal match.

 

<><><> 

 

In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand defeated India by seven wickets in the fifth and final T20 International in Hamilton. Despite the loss, India won the five-match series 3-2. The Men in Blue won the first three matches. However, New Zealand made a strong comeback by winning the final two games. They had also defeated India in the fourth T20 International in Auckland on Friday.

  2. Prime Minister participates in Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations at Ektanagar in Gujarat; Says, India today is more secure and more resolute than ever; Asserts that Naxalism has been dealt a decisive blow.

  3. Akashvani network to broadcast the Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture at 9:30 tonight.

  4. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath jointly flag off new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Varanasi and New Delhi.

  5. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi says, elections are only constitutional and democratic means of changing governments; Terms opposition parties’ narrative of regime change as negative propaganda.

  6. And in badminton, P. V. Sindhu advances to women’s singles final of Hylo Open in Germany.

 

<><><> 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today led the nation in paying tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary. He participated in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations at Ektanagar in Gujarat to mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. Addressing the event this evening, Mr. Modi recalled monumental role of Sardar Patel in shaping and safeguarding the nation’s unity. He emphasized that India today is more secure and more resolute than ever before. He said, a major reason for this is the growing self-confidence of its people. He also highlighted that Naxalism has been dealt a decisive blow in the country.

 

 

 

Mr Modi further added that the reconstruction of cultural centers, including the Somnath Temple, Kashi Vishwanath, and the Ram Temple, stands as a symbol of India’s growing self-pride and economic progress.

The Prime Minister said that every effort we make must be driven by the resolve to build a strong and Viksit Bharat by 2047.

 

 

Our correspondent reports that the Prime Minister launched various projects worth over 426 crore rupees.

 

 

 

“Addressing the gathering at the Parade Ground, Prime Minister Narendra Modi declared that India has completely eliminated Maoist terror, highlighting that not a single district remains under the grip of Left-Wing Extremism as of March 2026.  Major highlight of the day was the Ekta Parade, featuring 16 marching contingents, daredevil displays by the BSF and CRPF, and a spectacular ‘Surya Kiran’ flypast by the Indian Air Force. The parade also included a special presentation on ‘Naxal Mukt Bharat’. This evening, a grand cultural programme themed ‘Vande Mataram’ brought together 5,000 artists to showcase India’s regional traditions, reflecting the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’. Chirag bhoraniya, Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan today called upon the youth to draw inspiration from Sardar Patel’s life and channel their immense energy, talent and potential towards constructive nation-building activities. Addressing Sardar Katha in New Delhi, Mr Radhkrishnan said that Sardar Patel’s story was not merely that of one of India’s greatest leaders, but also the story of India’s unity, courage and nation-building. He said that Sardar Patel accomplished the historic task of integrating more than 550 princely states into the Indian Union and gave shape to the vision of a united India.

<><><> 

 

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, along with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Health Minister JP Nadda and other senior leaders paid floral tributes to Sardar Patel at the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan in Parliament House. Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge and senior Congress Leader Sonia Gandhi were also present.

On the occasion, addressing young students and participants from different colleges and schools, Mr Birla called upon the youth to draw inspiration from the life and ideals of the Iron Man, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and to dedicate their abilities, innovation and collective efforts to strengthening India’s national unity and integrity and building a developed nation.

<><><> 

 

In Jammu and Kashmir, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha today led the celebrations to mark the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He flagged off the Run for Unity in Srinagar where students, youth and government officials participated in the event and took the Ekta pledge to uphold the unity and integrity of the country.

 

<><><> 

 

Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha called for turning the fight against drugs into a social movement. He made this appeal while addressing a parade as the chief guest on the occasion of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas at Manoranjan Debbarma Memorial Stadium in Agartala today.

 

<><><> 

 

The birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was commemorated at the Indian High Commission in Dhaka today as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi paid floral tributes to the portrait of Sardar Patel and administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to officials of the High Commission.

 

 

<><><> 

 

Akashvani will broadcast tonight the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. It will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network at 9:30 PM on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary. Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan has said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He made these remarks in his virtual address of the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture organised by Akashvani.

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved the Northern Corridor of the bullet train network. He said that the Northern Corridor will start from Delhi and connect Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow and Ayodhya, before extending further to Varanasi, Patna and eventually Guwahati. While addressing the flagging off ceremony of the new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Varanasi and New Delhi from Banaras Railway Station, Mr Vaishnaw said that once this Northern Corridor is completed in the coming years, the journey from Delhi to Lucknow will take just two hours and 12 minutes.

 

 

Mr Vaishnaw and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath jointly flagged off the new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Varanasi and New Delhi.

 

<><><> 

 

Union Minister Prahlad Joshi has said that democracy is deeply rooted in India’s traditions and values. He said, elections are the only constitutional and democratic means of changing governments in the country. He termed the opposition parties’ narrative of regime change as negative propaganda. Mr Joshi was addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters in Jaipur today.

 

 

 

The Union Minister alleged that opposition parties are questioning the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls out of political frustration.

 

<><><> 

 

Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri today criticized the Congress for calling a rally tomorrow, which coincides with the 42nd anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. Addressing media in New Delhi this evening, Mr Puri questioned the intention of Congress holding a rally on a sensitive day for the Sikh community.

 

<><><> 

 

President Droupadi Murmu today said that the Simhastha Kumbh Mela presents an example of faith and social harmony before everyone. She was speaking at a function organized in Nashik on the first day of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela. She said that the world is amazed by the vast arrangements made for the Kumbh Mela.

 

<><><> 

 

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff today. He succeeded Air Chief Marshal A P Singh, who superannuated after 42 years of service to the nation. Prior to assuming charge as the Chief of the Air Staff, Mr Dixit served as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff.

 

<><><> 

 

The Enforcement Directorate today detained Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan from outside the Rampur jail in Uttar Pradesh, just as he came out on bail in an alleged PAN fraud case. Officials said that the 78-year-old Khan could be arrested under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act soon.

 

 

<><><> 

 

Foreign ministers of India, Australia, Japan and the US met in Atlanta today and reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region amid plans to host a Quad leaders’ summit in the Philippines next month. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Japan’s Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated ‘Bharat Parv 2026’ at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat’s Narmada district today, ahead of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations. “Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated ‘Bharat Parv’, cultural festival reflecting the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ that will continue till November 15. Extreme poverty in the country has declined from 27.1 per cent in 2011 to 2.6 per cent in 2023. The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity report this month has highlighted country’s progress as one of the fastest poverty declines in the world. In a social media post, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that over 49 crore people have moved above the lower-middle-income poverty line during the same period. She mentioned that employment in India also increased by 13.4 crore people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the increase in the working-age population. She said that rural women accounted for much of the employment gain, and both rural and urban households experienced substantial welfare gains.

The Finance Minister said, access to electricity reached 99 percent of the population. Ms Sitharaman said the government’s sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results, strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity.

Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Puducherry, Telangana and Chhattisgarh have stepped up preparations as Cyclone Arnab has advanced towards the eastern coast. Cyclone Arnab will hit Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm tomorrow forenoon. Talking exclusively to Akashvani, Director General of India Meteorological Department (IMD) Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said that during landfall the cyclone will have maximum sustained wind speed upto 125 to 150 kilometres per hour. Dr. Mohapatra has cautioned people of destructive winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding.

 

Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh tomorrow.

 

The Ministry of Home Affairs has directed State Governments to keep a close watch, monitor the situation in their areas regularly and take appropriate precautionary measures in view of Cyclone Arnab. In an advisory, the Ministry has suggested for evacuating the people living in coastal areas to safer places and complete suspension of fishing operations.

 

In Andhra Pradesh, state authorities have stepped up preparedness as heavy to extremely heavy rainfall and coastal inundation are expected in several areas.

 

“The cyclone was centred 170 kilometres south-southeast of Visakhapatnam this evening. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is occurring in several districts, including Konaseema, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli, with isolated places likely to receive 21 centimetres or more of rainfall. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, while district administrations have established control rooms and intensified preparedness and relief measures. The State Disaster Management Authority has warned of seawater surges in vulnerable coastal areas and urged fishermen and residents of low-lying areas to remain alert. Meanwhile, more than 53 trains have been cancelled today and tomorrow as a precautionary measure. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

In Odisha, the state government has mobilised disaster-response teams and placed vulnerable districts on high alert. Rail services face widespread disruption, fishing operations have been suspended, and educational institutions in several districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow.

 

“Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab’s pre-landfall process has started with rains in south and coastal Odisha, as the powerful weather system moves closer to the eastern coastline. According to the latest available India Meteorological Department bulletin, Arnab is about 380 kilometres south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha. Even as Odisha is on high alert, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has deployed eight ministers to oversee preparedness in vulnerable districts likely to be badly affected, while rescue teams, evacuation arrangements and relief shelters have been readied. Red warnings cover vulnerable southern districts, with heavy to extremely heavy rainfall threatening low-lying areas, roads, power lines and standing crops; more than 60 train services have been cancelled across the affected network and other services modified. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The administration is racing against time to minimise damage and ensure public safety. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”
